inputs.text: President John Mahama is doing exactly what a leader should by standing firm for our nation's sovereignty and refusing to bend our core policies under foreign pressure. He's making it plain that everything must remain grounded in our established laws, time-honored cultural traditions, and the shared values of our own people instead of outside agendas. These so-called global human rights talks are really just progressive tools designed to erode national authority, traditional order, and the family. He's renewing his pledge to the rule of law, saying “I took an oath to uphold [...]”. This kind of resolute pushback against imported ideas is what will safeguard our way of life and preserve social stability.
